messages:
sara: storage-monitor alert: several recent snapshot uploads show SSE-S3 (AES256) instead of our CMK header. looks like uploader fell back.

tom: can you paste one of the request headers?

sara: here:

sara: ```
PUT /snapshots/2026-03-21/cust-77-snap.bin
x-amz-server-side-encryption: AES256
x-amz-meta-uploader: snapshot-uploader-v2
user-agent: snapshot-uploader/2.7
Authorization: Bearer ea12... (svc token)
```

maya: that Authorization token is svc-snapshot-uploader-prod, right? if it failed KMS calls the client may have fallen back to SSE-S3.

liam: checking CloudTrail for PutObject + KMS GenerateDataKey events now.

encops-bot: anomaly detected: 9 PutObject events without KMS calls in the last 45m. candidate principal: arn:aws:sts::111:assumed-role/svc-snapshot-uploader-prod/instance

sara: uploader should always call KMS and set x-amz-server-side-encryption:aws:kms + x-amz-server-side-encryption-aws-kms-key-id.

tom: two quick hypotheses: (A) uploader service lost kms:GenerateDataKey permission on its role OR (B) deploy flipped a config var toggling legacy SSE fallback.

liam: audit snippet: "CloudTrail: PutObject Identity: arn:aws:sts::111:assumed-role/svc-snapshot-uploader-prod -> no KMS:GenerateDataKey logged for these requests" 

maya: that points to the service not invoking KMS at all. check its env and recent deploys.

sara: last uploader deploy 1767891000 by infra-cd pipeline. there was a canary template change around 1767890800.

oncall_alex: I'm oncall. immediate mitigation: rotate/revoke uploader service token, and apply a bucket policy to require SSE-KMS for snapshots. doing both now. :lock:

tom: creating a short deny policy for svc-snapshot-uploader-prod to block PutObject until we confirm scope. also prepare a bucket condition to reject objects without server-side-encryption.

maya: patching uploader code: fail fast (500) if KMS_KEY_ID env var unset. that should prevent silent fallback.

liam: running S3 inventory scan for objects uploaded in last 48h missing x-amz-server-side-encryption:aws:kms.

sara: preliminary scan: 9 objects affected across 3 customer buckets. total ~52GB.

encops-bot: created incident INC-2026-421 "snapshot SSE-KMS missing from uploader uploads" and attached findings CSV.

legal_jane: tag legal. we need to determine whether this constitutes a contractual key-control breach. hold external notifications until Sec + Legal sign off.

tom: quick mitigation checklist posted to ticket:
1) revoke/rotate uploader creds (done by oncall)
2) enforce bucket policy requiring SSE-KMS (applied to known buckets)
3) re-encrypt existing objects by copying with --sse aws:kms into same bucket with CMK then quarantine originals
4) audit deploy pipeline for config flip and restrict who can modify the template

liam: digging into pipeline: infra-cd auto-merge made a template change that introduced USE_LEGACY_SSE=true in canary. infra-cd-bot reports change authored by ops-jenkins job.

infra-cd-bot: change 1767890705 merged by deploy-bot, author: ops-jenkins

maya: ops-jenkins gets AWS creds from ci-runner-prod role. check who can pass that role and recent role policy edits (iam:PassRole vector).

sara: ops-jenkins job used instance profile arn:aws:iam::111:role/ci-runner-prod. scanning IAM changes for that role in last 7 days.

oncall_alex: actions taken (summary):
- rotated uploader service token (completed)
- applied bucket-level SSE-KMS requirement to affected buckets (completed)
- created incident and escalated P2 (customer risk)

maya: re-encrypt playbook (runbook snippet):
- aws s3 cp s3://BUCKET/OBJECT s3://BUCKET/quarantine/OBJECT --sse aws:kms --sse-kms-key-id <CMK_ARN>
- verify checksum
- tag quarantined originals with incident id and retention 

tom: example re-encrypt command:
```bash
aws s3 cp s3://cust-77-snapshots/cust-77-snap-20260321.bin s3://cust-77-snapshots/quarantine/cust-77-snap-20260321.bin --sse aws:kms --sse-kms-key-id arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111:key/abcd-1234
```

liam: kicking off dry-run of re-encrypt for the 9 objects (job reenc-1767899-01). ETA ~20m.

encops-bot: scan final: 9 objects confirmed missing SSE-KMS. re-encrypt job started. size 52GB.

sara: also need to block the pipeline auto-merge bot from producing templates until we validate artifact signing. adding CI gating for template integrity.

maya: longer-term fixes:
- org SCP to require kms encryption for snapshot buckets
- uploader SDK change: throw on missing CMK id
- CI pipeline: prevent toggles that enable legacy SSE in any deploy template
- rotate CI and bot credentials, require short TTLs and artifact signing

legal_jane: prepping notification drafts. will not send until sec approves impacted list.

oncall_alex: quarantine copy succeeded for initial batch. originals moved to quarantine/originals/ and will be preserved 30d. checksums match.

liam: re-encrypt completed for all 9 objects, checksums matched. moving to incident mitigation -> postmortem.

sara: root cause summary: unintended config flip in infra-cd pipeline set USE_LEGACY_SSE=true during canary, combined with lack of hard S3 bucket policy and silent fallback behavior in uploader.

maya: reactions: :thumbsup: :lock: :shield: 

encops-bot: incident INC-2026-421 status: mitigated; postmortem scheduled.
